text:
Maria Lopez: Hey folks — our private/VPC installer is failing during bootstrap. It can't pull some packages and model shards. Can we get an egress allowlist for the hosts below? Repro + logs included.

Raj Patel: Can you paste the exact error and a quick repro (curl/pip/apt)? Also which env (VPC, corp-proxy) is this on?

Maria Lopez: It's a customer VPC (air-gapped with explicit egress allowlist). Steps: 
1) Run ./install.sh --mode private
2) agent tries to fetch packages and model manifests

Observed errors:
```
pip install -r requirements.txt
> requests.exceptions.SSLError: [SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] certificate verify failed
curl https://models-cdn.redwood-internal.net/manifest.json --fail
curl: (35) error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:sslv3 alert certificate unknown
```

And an openssl check:
```
openssl s_client -connect telemetry.ingest-redwood.net:443 -servername telemetry.ingest-redwood.net
CONNECTED(00000003)
140736...:error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:sslv3 alert certificate unknown
---
no peer certificate available
```

Evan (ops-eng): That looks like TLS interception / SNI mismatch from their proxy. If the proxy is terminating TLS, we need the cert chain to validate or allow hostname passthrough. Can we get the hosts first so the customer can allow them?

Maria Lopez: Proposed host allowlist (please review/add):
- packages.pkg.redwood.ai (443)  -- our Python wheels and private pkg index
- models-cdn.redwood-internal.net (443) -- model manifests and small shards
- shards-us-west.s3.amazonaws.com (443) -- large model shard objects (S3 endpoint, sigv4)
- telemetry.ingest-redwood.net (443) -- metrics/usage/heartbeat
- auth.redwood.ai (443) -- OAuth/token endpoints
- registry.npmjs.org (443) -- npm dependencies used in examples
- ghcr.io (443) -- container images for bootstrap jobs
- api.docker.com / registry-1.docker.io (443) -- base images pulled by installer
- maven.central.repo (443) -- java deps for tests (if running JVM tests)

Raj Patel: Also add these for OS/package managers:
- deb.nodesource.com (443) -- nodejs apt repo
- dl.yarnpkg.com (443)
- storage.googleapis.com (443) -- some releases hosted on GCS

Infra Oncall Bot: @Maria Lopez I created ticket INF-4829 to track allowlist verification. Please include the customer's proxy type (explicit TLS intercept or allow SNI passthrough) and whether client certs are used.

Maria Lopez: Customer says the proxy is corporate TLS intercepting appliance (decrypt + re-encrypt). They do NOT want to disable interception. They can allow hostname passthrough for the above hosts OR install our root CA into the appliance. They asked for IP ranges to allow in firewall as they're strictly whitelisting outbound IPs only.

Evan (ops-eng): Providing IP ranges is brittle with CDNs. Recommend two options to customer: 
1) Allow TLS passthrough (port 443) for the hostnames above (SNI-based allowlist).
2) If only IP firewall allowed, provide minimal known IPs but warn they may change: e.g. S3 ranges for shard buckets (AWS ip-ranges), GitHub packages (140.82.0.0/16, 185.199.108.0/22 — customer should fetch provider IP lists).

Raj Patel: For their quick unblock, ask them to: 
- Temporarily allow SNI passthrough to packages.pkg.redwood.ai and telemetry.ingest-redwood.net and retry install.
- If they can't, install our customer-provided root CA in the TLS appliance (we can produce a cert bundle).

Maria Lopez: Customer asked for a single copy/paste hosts list for their network team. Can you confirm final recommended hostnames and any subpaths they should allow (e.g., /manifests, /shards)?

Evan (ops-eng): Final consolidated list (hostnames only, port 443):
packages.pkg.redwood.ai
models-cdn.redwood-internal.net
shards-us-west.s3.amazonaws.com
telemetry.ingest-redwood.net
auth.redwood.ai
registry.npmjs.org
ghcr.io
registry-1.docker.io
deb.nodesource.com
dl.yarnpkg.com
storage.googleapis.com

Notes for network team:
- Prefer SNI-based allowlist on port 443; do NOT terminate TLS for these hosts if possible.
- If TLS must be intercepted, ensure the appliance is configured to present a valid chain that validates against devices in the VPC, or install the appliance root CA across hosts.
- For S3 and CDN endpoints, allow AWS CIDR ranges for the region, but expect occasional CDNs/edge IP changes.
- If customer uses a strict IP-only policy, we can work with them to pin to a small set of IPs for a sprint but it is a support risk.

Support Bot: Ticket INF-4829 updated with consolidated host list and recommended mitigation steps. Assigned to Raj Patel and Evan (ops-eng).

Maria Lopez: Thanks — I'll forward this to the customer's network team and will post their response here. :thumbsup:
